I need it. After last week's picks, I need to go into hiding. It was awful. When you can't get over .500 with the straight-up picks, you know it's a bad week. I went 6-8 straight up and 3-11 against the spread. I could flip a coin and do better. Maybe my cats will make my picks next week. My season records are now 54-38-1 straight up and 37-54-2 against the spread. That is vile. Time to turn it around, so I am going to the dogs. Let them bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. Plus, New England seems to have found a groove on offense during a three-game winning streak, and both teams are in the top half of the league in EPA/Play on that side of the ball. So, this game could have a ton of offensive fireworks, which is great for bettors looking to wager on some anytime touchdown scorers. The total is all the way up at 50.5, and the Bears are currently a top-10 scoring offense while New England has put together three huge games with Drake Maye throwing 10 touchdowns during this winning streak. The Patriots are banged up quite a bit on offense, including receiver Romeo Doubs, who hauled in a score in the team’s Week 6 win over the New York Jets. Can A.J. Brown step up in his place after struggling with drops in his return from injured reserve? On the Bears side, Williams threw just one score in the 31-point showing in Week 6, but it’s possible that could change at home on Thursday. home.blurb: Coming out of Week 6, it looked as if Jonah Jackson was going to miss time with a hip injury. However, the right guard has bucked the trend and beaten the odds, leading to a major sigh of relief from quarterback Caleb Williams. Chicago’s offense still won’t be whole, as running back Kyle Monangai remains out with thumb/toe injuries. But the Bears having their standout right guard in place will lead to optimism. The Bears’ battle with the Patriots will be telling of where each franchise stands in their playoff pursuit. Having Jackson on the field would have Chicago feeling more confident about coming out on top. Jackson practiced in full on Wednesday and is entering Week 7’s battle against the New England Patriots without an injury designation, the team announced. Barring a sudden setback, Jackson should be cleared for Thursday Night Football. Chicago held a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice on Wednesday. Still, the fact Jackson earned the full tag shows the team’s confidence in him. The Bears will be still be paying close attention to Jackson and his hip, but the franchise is aware of how resilient the guard is. Jonah Jackson is key piece of Chicago Bears puzzle Entering Week 7, Jackson’s 83.7 grade from Pro Football Focus ranks sixth/77 guards . He has excelled in the run game, ranking sixth overall with a 81.5 mark. With elite right tackle Darnell Wright next to him, the Bears have found major success when running the ball on that side of the field. Chicago currently leads the league in rushing, averaging 160.7 yards per game. No marry who is carrying the rock, the Bears are confident knowing the blockers they’ll be running behind. When head coach Ben Johnson was hired, one of the team’s first moves was acquiring Jackson in a trade with the Los Angeles Rams. For all the flash, Johnson needs a stout offensive line for his gameplan to flourish. And he believes Jackson is the perfect fit at right guard for success. Want more articles like this? Caleb Williams returned to action for the Chicago Bears in Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, re-taking the field after missing each of the last three games with a hamstring injury. Williams was excellent in the Bears' 31-23 win, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts for 305 yards and one touchdown through the air. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. home.blurb: The Falcons' offense looked outmatched by the Bears defense in the first quarter, while Chicago was clicking on all cylinders. Caleb Williams lit Atlanta up in his return from a hamstring injury, going 30/36 for 305 yards and one touchdown. Overall, the Falcons committed three fumbles, two from wide receiver Zachariah Branch. The rookie return man did bounce back with a few nice plays late, but it was tough to overcome the miscues. The Atlanta Falcons laid another egg in front of their fans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, losing 31-23 to the Chicago Bears to fall to 2-4 overall and 0-3 at home this season. Michael Penix Jr. got off to another slow start but did his best to keep the Falcons in the game late. Penix finished with 225 passing yards and three touchdowns, but his fumble in the final minutes ended Atlanta's comeback attempt. The other big story of the day was the injury to Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels , who was carted off with a neck injury in a scary moment. McCarthy starting for Giants Pittsburgh Steelers WR DK Metcalf (L) and New Orleans Saints RB Alvin Kamara | Brian Fluharty - Imagn Images and Michael Owens - Getty Images | Graphic by Adam Patrick Shayne Kubas Wed, October 21, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers will make NFL history this week, as will their opponent, the New Orleans Saints. For the first time in the league's long existence, a regular season game will be played in France. Paris, to be exact. After nearly 20 years since the Dolphins and Giants played the first regular season game outside of North America, the NFL's international footprint grows larger every year. As interesting as all of that is, the football played on the field is what really matters. Pittsburgh enters Week 7 with a 4-2 record, barely beating the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime a week ago. The Saints, meanwhile, climbed to 2-4 after a bizarre 34-27 win over the Giants. Both teams have plenty of flaws they are hoping to correct as the season goes on, but the Steelers are favored for a reason. As the game approaches, we will have all of the important details you need to know. Injury reports, weather reports, how to watch, storylines, and more. So bookmark this page and come back throughout the week! How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints in Week 7 Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 9:30 a.m. EST TV Network: NFL Network Announcers: Dave Pasch (Play-by-Play), Kurt Warner and Jason Kelce (Color Analysts), Molly McGrath (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 7 Steelers injury reports will appear here as they become available New Orleans Saints Injury Report for Week 7 Saints injury reports will appear here as they become available Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs New Orleans Saints Week 7 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: TBD Wind Speed: TBD Precipitation: TBD Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 7 Will the Steelers continue leaning on the passing game despite missing multiple playmakers? Despite missing multiple receivers heading into their Week 6 matchup with the Buccaneers, the Steelers chose to make the passing game the focal point of the offense. While they ultimately came away with the victory, it was an ugly mess for much of the contest. Aaron Rodgers put up a solid 253 yards through the air, but it took him a whopping 49 pass attempts to get there. He was the definition of a checkdown merchant , with just five of those 49 passes traveling beyond 10 yards, according to Next Gen Stats . It seemed as though Mike McCarthy didn't have faith that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle could succeed against the Buccaneers' stout run defense. Still, the Steelers can't win games against good teams with that offensive approach. The Saints could be a team that they can once again get away with it against, but it's something to monitor. Which team will handle the international trip better? There has been plenty of discourse surrounding how to handle playing across the pond ever since the NFL's International Series took shape. We saw the Rams be criticized for arriving in Australia right before their Week 1 disaster against the 49ers, who had been down under for days at that point. In the Steelers case, they are taking the route of trying to make the week feel as normal as possible, choosing to fly out on Thursday evening. Meanwhile, the Saints arrived in France on Monday, so they will be well adjusted by game time on Sunday. Will the contrasting strategies make any difference? Only time will tell. Can the Steelers pass rush come alive against a struggling Saints offensive line? The Steelers' pass rush has long been the strength of their defense, but they haven't been as effective on a down-to-down basis this season. According to Sumer Sports , Pittsburgh ranks just 23rd in pressure percentage at 37.4%. They do rank ninth in sacks with 16, so they have managed to get the QB on the ground at an above-average level. Still, they aren't causing as much disruption as they need to be, considering the names in that group. T.J. Watt has cooled off after a hot start, Alex Highsmith isn't having his best season, and Nick Herbig has made splash plays but hasn't been as dominant as he was last season. The interior has been hot and cold, with Cam Heyward remaining a consistent presence while the other pieces have been hit-or-miss. With the Saints missing star left tackle Kaleb Banks, this is an opportunity for them to really hit their stride. If they don't, it may be time to worry. McCarthy starting for Giants Saints Rookie Report: Week 7 preview vs. the Steelers BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Jeremiah Wright #65 of the New Orleans Saints reacts against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a nearly disastrous loss to the New York Giants, the New Orleans Saints are facing another must-win situation against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the game will be played overseas in Paris. In that Week 6 game, the Saints' rookies put on some nice performances, and Week 7 may be the breakout game for this class. WR Jordyn Tyson Finally, we can talk about Jordyn Tyson. Although his availability for Sunday's game is up in the air, he did travel with the team, which means there's a chance he plays. The Saints' offense has had a number of issues this season, and although Tyson will not fix everything, he is a massive upgrade over Bryce Lance. The injuries have been demoralizing, to say the least, but Tyson is an extremely talented player who can be one of the best WRs in the NFL. Although I would expect a small sample size if he does play, we may finally see him on the field. DT Christen Miller Although this was another game where the Saints went with other DT options over Miller, he did get on the field and helped shut down New York's running game. In Week 7, the Saints face a much better rushing attack led by Jaylen Warren, so they will have to rely on Miller a bit more. TE Oscar Delp Against the Giants, Delp had his best game so far. He made some really important blocks that significantly helped the run game and had two catches. It wasn't an incredible performance by any means, but one that could lead to more snaps for Delp. Delp is likely going to be in the same exact role for Week 7. OG Jeremiah Wright After Cesar Ruiz left the game with an injury, rookie Jeremiah Wright was thrown into the lineup, and suddenly the run game looked great. Could this be a coincidence? Maybe. But it was clear that lanes were being opened up that the running backs could easily take advantage of. He got pushed back and beat at times, any rookie would, but overall, it was exactly what you wanted to see in his first real game. Now with Ruiz's health in question, and the fact Wright's debut was positve, the Saints must start him in Week 7. Might as well see what you have with Wright in a full game. WR Bryce Lance This was an up-and-down game for Lance. He once again had some head-scratching moments, including a drop, but he also scored the first touchdown of his young career. With Tyson's return, Lance may be demoted to a more blocking role, but that may be better for now, especially as he develops. WR Barion Brown I thought Barion Brown had the best game of his career as well. He had some really nice returns and made a nice contested catch that may have been an interception if he didn't get to the ball. Brown will likely fall to WR5 on the depth chart, but just like Lance, that's perfectly fine. RB CJ Donaldson Another up-and-down game, Donaldson had some really nice runs to begin the game and fought for some tough yards. He nearly scored the first touchdown of his career, but was called back after his knee was down short. His blocking was also good, which was needed against the blitzes. Then we get to the fumble. The Giants' comeback started after Donaldson fumbled, and that put a stain on this performance. Not sure if Donaldson will see fewer snaps in Week 7, but it's something to monitor. OT Mason Murphy Murphy did not come into this game like last week, but after Asim Richards clear struggles against the Giants, it may be time for New Orleans to try something new. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was once again an impact player on special teams, which is exactly why the Saints drafted him.

Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. home.headline: Injury Hampers Steelers RB Before Saints Game
home.blurb: PITTSBURGH — Rico Dowdle was included on the Pittsburgh Steelers' injury report once again on Wednesday, now dealing with a knee injury. He was listed as a limited participant as Mike McCarthy's team prepares to take on the New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday. Dowdle had dealt with a toe injury suffered in Week 2 against the New England Patriots, which kept him out until the Steelers' 26-19 road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Sunday. Dowdle had seven carries for 40 yards in that matchup. Injury Hampers Steelers RB Before Saints Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings J.J. McCarthy starting for Giants Injury Hampers Steelers RB Before Saints Game Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle at practice on Oct. 8, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Brendan Howe Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:47 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Dowdle joined the Steelers with plans of splitting the workload with Jaylen Warren, who has emerged as Pittsburgh's top ballcarrier this season. "He's been very underrated in this league for a long time," tight end Pat Freiermuth said of Warren after a 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 4. "I go back to when PQ (Patrick Queen) was in Baltimore and he came here, I'm pretty sure he said when Jaylen was a rookie (or in his) second-year, that he's the hardest to tackle in the NFL. … Every time we get him the ball, he makes a good play." Still, the Steelers will need to keep Warren fresh if they want him to be effective late into the season. Dowdle being in the fold helps that. picks.headline: 49ers at Falcons early predictions: Best Week 7 bets to target
picks.blurb: Morris is surely equipped to counter Atlanta's attack, having led the same core from 2024-25 as head coach. But a San Francisco defense that tops the league in defensive expected points added per play on rushing attempts will be in for its stiffest test yet against the All-Pro ball carrier. On the other side of the ball, Brock Purdy will look to maintain sky-high efficiency despite mounting attrition at wide receiver . Falcons vs 49ers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: 49ers -4.5 Moneyline: 49ers -230; Falcons +190 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Falcons vs 49ers USA TODAY expert picks Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: 49ers 35, Falcons 24 How San Francisco's surprising defense handles Robinson is sure to be one of the most compelling storylines in this game. But mitigating any damage might not fall on that unit alone. Chicago managed to minimize Robinson's role by stringing together long drives and holding onto the ball for more than 40 minutes. Given how prolific San Francisco's offense is at working the intermediate area - and how badly Atlanta's defense struggles in that area - the 49ers could leave the Falcons in a problematic position by racing out to an early lead and controlling the terms of the game. Adam Kaufman: 49ers 30, Falcons 23 At some point, San Francisco's injuries have to catch up with it, right? The 49ers keep answering that question with another win to stay unbeaten, although Mike Evans' latest injury creates another challenge on a short week before traveling to Atlanta. Fortunately, Brock Purdy still has Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle to help keep the offense moving. I like those options against a Falcons secondary that has struggled. The Falcons' path is straightforward: feed Bijan Robinson, keep Purdy watching and prevent Michael Penix Jr. from having to rescue the game with difficult throws. That should keep Atlanta competitive, but I'm still expecting San Francisco to execute more consistently and take advantage of a mistake or two. Falcons vs 49ers picks roundup Sports Illustrated : 49ers -3 "Until the Falcons' secondary gets healthy, they're going to get torched by any competent quarterback, and this week they have to take on an MVP candidate in Brock Purdy, which will be the Falcons' toughest test yet." The Athletic : Falcons +3.5 "Spoiler alert: the San Francisco 49ers are again dealing with injuries." BetMGM : Falcons are intriguing underdog "San Francisco travels to Atlanta on a short week while the Falcons get a third consecutive home game. ... picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Falcons odds: The most difficult game on the schedule yet | Niners Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A San Francisco 49ers Community Niners Nation October 21, 2026 Niners Nation Notifications Notifications Sections Golden Nuggets By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds San Francisco 49ers Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Sections Expand Golden Nuggets By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications San Francisco 49ers Odds We highlight why this game is difficult for the 49ers The San Francisco 49ers are 6-0 heading into Week 6. For the first time in a few weeks, they “lost” against the spread on Monday. The Niners are still 5-2 against the spread, with the NFL’s second-highest margin of victory at 11.2. They’re also tied for a league-high average margin of victory. So, when media members ask this: I would say the answer is no. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The matchup against the Atlanta Falcons always looked like a scheduled loss, if there ever was one. The 49ers are 3-point road favorites, with the total on the game sitting at 49.5 on FanDuel Sportsbook . A high total and a low spread hint at a coin-flip game. We’ll see if Mike Evans plays. On the outside, it makes more sense to give Evans two weeks off so the Achilles soreness goes away and allows Evans to complete a game. But Kyle Shanahan seems to be putting the ball in Evans’s court. If the veteran feels healthy enough to play, he’ll play, even if the team knows they could lose him mid-game. There’s familiarity here, as Raheem Morris takes on his old team. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich is one of the best in the league and worked with Shanahan in Atlanta a decade ago, not to mention as Morris’s defensive coordinator. Morris will need to find a way to limit Drake London, who has the 8th-highest target share among all NFL receivers. The Falcons throw it to London over 28% of the time. London is 11th in EPA per target. Not far behind London is his teammate Jahan Dotson, who is 14th in EPA per target. Tight end Kyle Pitts is fifth in EPA per target among tight ends. Atlanta is not short on weapons, and we haven’t even gotten to their biggest threat. Bijan Robinson is second in the NFL, averaging 5.77 yards per carry. He averages more yards after contact (4.64) than a good chunk of running backs do per carry. Robinson is a walking highlight who is heavily involved in Atlanta’s passing attack. Michael Penix is limited when it comes to being mobile, so that should work in the Niners favor. If there’s one person you’d want to attempt to slow down the Falcons, it’s the coach who drafted most of these players and watched them practice for the past few years: Raheem Morris. On the other side of the ball, no team has been better against the run than the Falcons defense. They’re first in EPA per rush and sixth in rushing success rate. Atlanta has allowed the third-fewest 10+ yard runs and is seventh in the percentage of runs they stuff. They make teams one-dimensional. This will be a Brock Purdy game. The Falcons won’t blitz Purdy nearly as often as Washington does, but they get pressure with four. That’s a big difference. Atlanta is fourth in pressure rate despite blitzing 23.7% of the time (26th in the NFL). You can throw on this defense. Atlanta is 20th and 21st in EPA per pass and passing success rate. Caleb Williams carved up the Dirty Birds for over 300 passing yards a week ago. A good chunk of those came in the first half. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had him a day. Tyler Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He threw for only 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw two touchdowns. Huntley was efficient in Week 5 at Atlanta. He only threw for 201 yards, but completed 75% of his passes and threw for two touchdowns. Rashod Bateman and Zay Flowers combined for 13 receptions for 115 yards. The week before, Tyler Shough threw the ball 48 times for 286 yards. Chris Olave had 116 yards. Of course, it’s far-fetched to imagine the Niners having a 100-yard receiver without Evans, but Shanahan has a full week to scheme up the non-Evans wideouts. A short road week with an early start on the East Coast, potentially without your leading receiver, against a team that has lost back-to-back games where they feel like they should have won. And the familiarity, paired with the weapons the Falcons have, makes this an intriguing game and a difficult schedule spot for a 6-0 team that could be feeling fat and happy a week away from the bye. David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard reported that Bosa said two weeks ago he expected to return before the 49ers' Week 8 bye. Samuel will likely miss Sunday's game, while Evans aggravated his Achilles during the second quarter of Monday night's game and didn't return. home.blurb: Atlanta Falcons Add Arctos as Limited Partner Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE NEW YORK – Oct. 20, 2026 – Arthur M. Blank, Atlanta Falcons Owner and Chairman, announced the addition of Arctos, a business of KKR, as a limited partner to the organization's ownership group following approval from the NFL's full ownership at league meetings today in New York. Today's transaction was for a 7.5 percent stake in the team. Arctos has also committed to purchasing an additional 2.5 percent stake at a later date, subject to a separate vote of NFL ownership at the time. Arctos joins the current group of limited partners that includes Brian Barker, Rosalind Brewer, Ron Canakaris, Dominique Dawes, Warrick Dunn, Doug Hertz, Alan Kestenbaum, Edward Mendel, Will Packer, Derek Smith and Rashaun Williams. "We are pleased to welcome the team at Arctos to our ownership group as a limited partner," said Blank. "Arctos has an impressive track record and has garnered tremendous respect across the sports landscape for their expertise and business acumen. Most importantly, they align with our Core Values and share our vision for continued investment in the organization and our surrounding community. "Arthur Blank has been instrumental in transforming Atlanta into one of the premier sports and entertainment destinations in the country, and the Falcons have been at the heart of that transformation," said Chad Hutchinson, Partner at Arctos. "We're honored to join the organization as a limited partner and excited to support Arthur and his team as they continue to build on that legacy for the city and its fans." The vote on the Atlanta Falcons new limited partner occurred today in New York; Arctos has been approved effective immediately and the transaction is expected to close later this month. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published 12 hours ago LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football WNBA Finals live updates Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings World Series preview Champions League results J.J. McCarthy starting for Giants 3 Bold predictions for the Browns against the Titans in Week 7 Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns march into Week 7 with an AFC North division lead and momentum behind them again. They are starting a softer stretch of the schedule but remain focused on the task ahead, which is the Tennessee Titans. Despite winning their first game in Week 6, the Titans are better than they have played. The Browns can win this game, though, if they keep up their defensive aggressiveness and make significant second-half adjustments. Todd Monken and his staff have risen to the occasion in every game, but this could be their first complete game in 2026 if they execute the way they are capable of. We said this is a poor Titans team, but there is still a game to be played, and we have some bold predictions to share ahead of it. Jared Verse gets his first sack of the season This is a wild thing to think about, but heading into Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans, Jared Verse is without a sack this season. Equally, Myles Garrett has also gone without a sack, but he has been on injured reserve. Fair or unfair, Verse is going to be linked to Garrett, and that means expectations will always be high. The Titans' offensive line is not the best unit, they are going to give up pressures, and it is time for Verse to capitalize on that. Jerry Jeudy finds the endzone Jerry Jeudy has seen him get more and more reps and big-time targets since Week 4 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In Week 6, he made a pivotal catch-and-run that set up the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt. Deshaun Watson and Todd Monken have spoke highly of Jeudy this past week and he seems poised for another boost to his role. In Week 7 against he Titans, he can take advantage of their poor secondary and find the endzone for the first time this season. Browns secure at least five sacks Titans quarterback Cam Ward has had a rough start to the season and it has Tennessee sitting with a record of 1-5. He has a tendency to hold onto the ball, be reckless with it, and I think that has the Browns poised to have a big week on the defensive side of the ball. You cannot always count on turnovers, but you can count on Mike Rutenberg being aggressive on defense. One way he will do that is by getting after Ward, and I think that is where the Browns are most productive in the form of securing at least five sacks. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 21, 2026, 5:07 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans are seeking their first consecutive win since 2022 after a victory over the Indianapolis Colts. Tennessee's offense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game, and quarterback Cam Ward had career lows in his last outing. Can the Tennessee Titans win twice in a row? That’s no small feat for an organization that hasn’t won consecutive games since 2022. But Tennessee’s 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts in NFL Week 6 quieted the storm after an 0-5 start. Now, the Titans (1-5) can prove it wasn’t a fluke when it hosts the Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Nissan Stadium on Oct. 25 (noon CT, CBS). The Browns are 1.5-point favorites. They lost last year's meeting 31-29 after Tennessee running back Tony Pollard rushed for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdowns. Questions remain for quarterback Cam Ward and the Titans' offense, who were bailed out by the defense and special teams against the Colts . Ward’s 11 completions and 102 yards passing against the Colts were career lows, and Tennessee still ranks last in the NFL in yards per game (236.3) and tied for last in points per game (14.0). Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cleveland Browns stat to know Other than the Baltimore Ravens ’ opening touchdown drive last week, the Browns surrendered three points and 169 yards of total offense to finish a 13-10 victory. Cleveland hasn’t been atop the AFC North this late in the season since 2014. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Browns Tennessee spent offseason resources beefing up its pass rush for coach Robert Saleh’s defensive scheme. The results finally surfaced with six sacks and 25 pressures against the Colts. Doing that again could hamper quarterback Deshaun Watson and the Browns, who have surrendered a league-high 24 sacks in six games. Cleveland left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber are both rookies. Titans eighth-year veteran Jeffery Simmons is arguably the NFL’s best defensive tackle. He has a team-high four sacks and 26 hurries. Where Cleveland Browns have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s passing offense is the NFL’s worst at 153.5 yards per game, and the Browns rank eighth in passing defense at 205.2 yards per game. Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward anchors a Cleveland secondary that ranks sixth in coverage grade at 71.1, according to Pro Football Focus. Cornerback Myles Harden has five passes defended this season. The Titans likely won’t win another game with a blocked punt return and four second-half field goals like they did against the Colts. If the Browns limit Cam Ward’s explosive plays downfield — they had six pass breakups against the Ravens — then Tennessee will struggle to score. Cam Ward has developed a go-to target in rookie receiver Carnell Tate, which is good. But receivers beyond Tate (44 targets) and Wan’Dale Robinson (37) aren’t that involved. Running back Tyjae Spears has more targets (17) than receiver Calvin Ridley (five). Elic Ayomanor has shown flashes of playmaking, but he’s averaging two targets the past four games and had a bad drop against the Colts. Score prediction: Browns 21, Titans 10 Ward’s limitations are clear through six games, giving Cleveland’s secondary a near-perfect blueprint. If nothing pops for Tennessee’s offense, the scoring woes will continue. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? away.headline: Browns’ latest injury update raises concerns ahead of Titans matchup
away.blurb: The Cleveland Browns are missing several notable players from practice ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . Camryn Justice of News 5 reported on six total players expected to be out for Wednesday practice: Delpit would be a big miss for the Browns, with one interception, one sack, and 25 combined tackles this year. Luckily for the Browns, they added depth at safety in the draft, and rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to emerge in recent weeks, with 24 tackles and just two receptions allowed this season. The Browns have some insurance at the position while Delpit works toward a return. Carson Schwesinger has been a defensive star for the Browns this season. Unfortunately, Schwesinger has been dealing with an ankle injury in recent weeks. The injury kept him out of practice most of last week ahead of the Ravens matchup, and he was limited in Friday's final practice. With Schwesinger missing Wednesday's practice, the Browns appear to be taking a similar approach this week. However, if his performance against the Ravens is any indication, Schwesinger should be available against the Titans. Grant Delpit is one of the Browns' key defensive players and was injured after being accidentally struck by teammate Derek Barnett during a tackle attempt on Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Delpit is listed as having a shoulder injury as well as a concussion. Delpit is the most uncertain name on the Browns' injury report, as he sustained the concussion during Sunday's matchup against Baltimore. The NFL's concussion protocol can be difficult to navigate, and his absence from Wednesday's practice raises questions about his availability this Sunday. Elgton Jenkins has anchored the Browns' offensive line at center this season and has been a bright spot for the position group. Jenkins was listed with a knee injury ahead of Wednesday's practice after playing every offensive snap against the Ravens in Week 6. While his absence is worth monitoring, Jenkins' ability to play through last week's matchup is encouraging. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday. The Browns' injury report remains long, but it shows some encouraging signs compared to last week's report ahead of the Ravens matchup. Mason Graham and Quinshon Judkins, who both missed the Ravens game, returned to practice, with signs pointing to both potentially returning to action against the Titans. While Delpit's status is concerning, the team has some depth at safety to help offset a potential absence. Meanwhile, Schwesinger and Jenkins have shown they can play through injuries, giving Cleveland reason to be optimistic heading into Sunday's matchup. away.headline: Denzel Boston limited at Cleveland Browns practice with injury
away.blurb: The 6-foot-4 pass catcher was still able to practice in a limited capacity, which is a good sign for his availability on Sunday when the Browns take on the Baltimore Ravens. The second-round pick in April's draft leads the NFL with 20.6 yards per reception, while his 330 yards and 3 touchdowns are the best among all rookies. Boston has tallied 16 catches through the first five games of the year and has been a big part of the Browns starting the season at 3-2, which has them tied for second place in the AFC North. However, after pulling in 3 catches for 46 yards and a touchdown against the New York Jets, Boston popped up on Cleveland's injury report on Wednesday with a foot issue. Throughout the year, Boston has made an early impression on the NFL, displaying why he was such a key piece of Jedd Fisch's offense in the head coach's first two seasons on Montlake. "Not making things too big, just keeping the main thing the main thing," Boston said of his poise and early success . "And also just understanding the camaraderie that we built around the building, having the trust that he's going to go make that play or he's going to go make that play. I think it just comes from a great locker room, a brotherhood, and an understanding of everyone's here for their purpose and everyone's going to fulfill their purpose when the time comes." The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle), who didn't practice Thursday or Friday. He has six tackles so far this season. The Ravens also have other offensive line injuries to monitor with guards Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) both questionable to play. They were limited throughout the week. Wide receivers Zay Flowers (toe) and Rashod Bateman (shoulder) are good to go with no injury designation. Flowers was limited Thursday and Friday but Bateman returned to full participation. Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could return from injured reserve after he suffered a wrist injury in Week 1 in Indianapolis. Lane had three full days of practice this week and is listed as questionable. He would have to be removed from injured reserve this weekend to play. While the Ravens could be at full strength at receiver, they're short at tight end with rookie Matt Hibner (hand) ruled out for Sunday's game. He didn't practice this week. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday. The Browns' injury report remains long, but it shows some encouraging signs compared to last week's report ahead of the Ravens matchup. Mason Graham and Quinshon Judkins, who both missed the Ravens game, returned to practice, with signs pointing to both potentially returning to action against the Titans. Meanwhile, Schwesinger and Jenkins have shown they can play through injuries, giving Cleveland reason to be optimistic heading into Sunday's matchup. home.headline: Gun involved in practice ‘incident’ that got Titans lineman Jordan Elliott released: reports
home.blurb: A to Z Sports further reported that Elliott stormed out of the locker room upset . Released Titans defensive lineman Jordan Elliott attempted to retrieve a firearm from his vehicle following a dispute with a teammate last Thursday, leading to the team cutting him Tuesday, according to reports. The Titans only acknowledged an “incident” at the team facility Oct. 15 in their statement regarding their decision to cut the 28-year-old, who was inactive for the Week 6 win over the Colts. Elliott, who signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the team in free agency, had a confrontation with offensive lineman JC Latham during practice Thursday, according to KPRC2 in Houston. The seventh-year veteran would be told to leave, and he reportedly took off his pads on the sidelines and left the team’s training facility to head to his car. Security cameras captured Elliott going to his car in an attempt to grab his gun, per KPRC2, before teammate John Franklin-Myers dissuaded him from doing any further. A source told KPRC2 that Elliott has been dealing with family issues that carried over into the workplace, and the Metro Nashville Police Department told A to Z Sports that no incident report had been filed. “This was so crazy,” an NFL source said told KPRC2. “Jordan has been having a lot of problems away from the building and obviously he brought it to work with him. There was no reason for him to go off like that. Everyone thought that was wild. To overreact like that is absolutely crazy. “We’re just glad that no one got hurt and it’s over.” Elliott practiced Wednesday and Thursday with no injury designation before not practicing Friday due to what the team labeled as non-injury related/personal reason. Coach Robert Saleh said last Friday that Elliott “was dealing with some personal stuff,” and the team made the lineman one of their inactives for the game. Elliott, who followed Saleh from the 49ers to the Titans, had appeared in each of the previous five games, starting one while logging 11 combined tackles. His career began with four seasons with the Browns after being selected in the third round of the 2020 Draft before two seasons with San Francisco. The nature of his Titans release certainly raises questions about his NFL future.

It seems like every week a big favorite is being upset, and Week 6 had two of them as the Los Angeles Rams (12.5-point favorites) lost outright at home to the Arizona Cardinals while the Indianapolis Colts (seven-point favorites) lost an AFC South battle with the previously winless Tennessee Titans. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. The Vikings, as we've mentioned, are one of three teams in the NFL who are still undefeated at 5-0, along with the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers. The Chiefs climbed to 5-0 by beating the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, while the Niners can get to 6-0 if they defeat the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. The Vikings have done this despite being fairly anemic on offense, thanks to the performance of their defensive and special teams units. In their last game, they overcame two red zone turnovers to defeat the New Orleans Saints by a score of 23-13 in a game that they played without left tackle Christian Darrisaw and wide receiver Jordan Addison, and saw tight end T.J. Hockenson go out on the second play of the game with a concussion. The sportsbooks have spoken, folks, and the Vikings are pretty significant favorites to push their record to 6-0 this week when they face off against the Colts. away.blurb: Four key injured players on the Vikings offense — left tackle Christian Darrisaw, tight end T.J. Hockenson, receiver Jordan Addison and running back Jordan Mason — fully practiced Wednesday afternoon, the team’s first session out of the bye. Darrisaw suffered at least the third concussion of his six-year Vikings career when he left the Oct. 4 win over the Dolphins. Hockenson hit his head on the Superdome turf on the third snap in New Orleans and did not return. Mason’s return would come at a good time for a Vikings run game that lacks punch. They have leaned heavily on 31-year-old starter Aaron Jones Sr., who handled a career-high 28 touches for 117 yards from scrimmage in the Oct. 11 win in New Orleans. But the Vikings have averaged just 3.8 yards per carry (21st) and have run for 28 first downs (28th). Mason, 27, technically has a three-week practice window before he needs to be activated from injured reserve, but O’Connell said after the Sept. 11 thumb injury that the Colts game was the initial hope for his return. Mason played through the injury and took a team-high 15 carries for 59 rushing yards and a touchdown in the Week 1 win over Green Bay. Only three Vikings players needed limited reps: receiver Justin Jefferson (ankle), right tackle Brian O’Neill (knee) and cornerback James Pierre (foot). After practice, Jefferson said his sprained right ankle that caused him to all but seven snaps of two games against the Bucs and Dolphins is doing “good.” He still needed limited reps in practice. The Minnesota Vikings are reaping the benefits of the bye week. Darrisaw and Hockenson remained in the concussion protocol during practice, but their full participation is the “final phase” toward clearance if they respond well, O’Connell said. “Hopefully getting C.D. and T.J. back in there will allow us to open up kind of the full run game,” O’Connell said, “and being in a little bit more of attack mode.” Addison is “good to go,” O’Connell said, indicating he’s expected to play Sunday vs. the Colts. He played through a hamstring strain against the Dolphins, but missed the Saints game. Addison ranks third on the team with 163 receiving yards in four games. Coordinator Wes Phillips said Mason ran “explosively” in camp this summer. “We were really excited about Jordan throughout the offseason,” Phillips said Tuesday. “I’ve mentioned before how good a shape he came in and that was really on his own accord. He felt like he was a little bit heavier than he wanted to be last year.” “It’s feeling better and better every single day,” Jefferson said Wednesday. “You still wake up with those aching pains like everybody does.” Cornerback Charles Demmings, the rookie fifth-round pick, was a full participant Wednesday for the first time since straining a hamstring Sept. 27 in Tampa Bay. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. away.blurb: The Buccaneers are running out of time to turn their season around. Entering Week 7, the team is 1-5, and if they want to make it back into the playoffs they need to start winning games. Unfortunately, Irving landed on the injury report for Wednesday's practice. Irving was listed as a DNP due to an illness that is going around the locker room. Mayfield officially returned to practice, which is good news for his availability in Week 7 as he looks to finally make his return. The Buccaneers were also without their backup running back in Week 6, as Sean Tucker did not play due to a quad injury against the Minnesota Vikings, leaving Tampa Bay to rely almost solely on Bucky Irving. The Buccaneers will visit the Carolina Panthers on Sunday and they need to secure a win.

away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Buccaneers Give ‘Encouraging’ Injury Update on QB Baker Mayfield for Panthers Game
home.blurb: Buccaneers Have Return Date in Mind for QB Baker Mayfield: Report Buccaneers Give ‘Encouraging' Injury Update on QB Baker Mayfield for Panthers Game Unlock the latest Heavy on Buccaneers news — direct to your inbox. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers might have their own version of "The Gloved One " at quarterback as they kick off NFC South play on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers . " Baker Mayfield is back at Bucs practice today, wearing a glove on his throwing hand as he tests his injured thumb," Fox Sports NFL reporter Greg Auman wrote on his official X account on Wednesday. "First step toward returning to the field. Taking snaps, throwing as well … Todd Bowles said it was ‘encouraging' to see what Baker Mayfield was able to do today in his first practice. They'll evaluate his progress Thursday and move from there." The Buccaneers are 1-2 with undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels starting for Mayfield and 1-5 heading into the Panthers game — yet somehow still very much in the playoff race because the NFC South is so bad. "Bucs coach Todd Bowles said he anticipates making a decision about quarterback Baker Mayfield on Friday," ESPN's Jenna Laine wrote on X . "He said he threw the ball well today and did well in what he was asked to do. They split reps up. A big thing will be how he feels tomorrow after a day of practice." "Bucs coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield was ‘effective' and it was ‘encouraging' how he practiced today," Tampa Bay Times NFL reporter Rick Stroud wrote on his official X account. "He played with a glove on his right hand and felt comfortable." Jalon Daniels, Bucs Blew Lead Against Steelers Daniels is coming off a disheartening 26-19 home overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. The rookie went 22-of-43 passing for 164 yards, 1 touchdown, and 2 interceptions. Daniels threw both interceptions in the fourth quarter as the Buccaneers blew a 16-3 lead over the last 15 minutes of regulation. Daniels went 19-of-25 for 189 yards, 1 touchdown, and no interceptions in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys , plus 23 rushing yards. Bucs Paying Big Money for Mayfield to Sit The Buccaneers dropped a ton of money on Mayfield right before the season — a 3-year, $165 million contract extension that ties the two entities together for the foreseeable future. "The Bucs and Baker Mayfield agreed to terms on a three-year contract extension," The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote on his official X account on September 9. " The sides recently re-engaged and Mayfield is now signed through 2029." That money paid for an 0-3 start before Mayfield hurt his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. Now, Jackson's status for Week 7 is up in the air, though oddsmakers have set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set at -148 to win this game, a sign that oddsmakers are bracing for Jackson to return from his two-game absence. After Jackson was ruled out for Week 6, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter gave a rather vague update on the star quarterback's status. "It's day by day, I would say," Minter said ahead of Week 6. "And I think it's just a decision for his best interest. And that's really what every decision's always going to be about." Jackson was injured in the first half of Baltmore's Week 4 win over Tennessee and did not return. He had thrown multiple scores in that game, giving the Ravens a huge cushion and they went on to win with Tyler Huntley at the helm. Huntley then received the start in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons and played a really solid game to lead the Ravens to a win. He completed 24 of his 32 pass attempts for 201 yards and two scores and added a touchdown on the ground in an overtime win. At 4-1, the Ravens were in a great spot in the AFC North, and ESPN's Adam Schefter had reported that Jackson has a realistic chance to return in Week 6. However, the two-time MVP did not practice all week ahead of the game against Cleveland, and was eventually ruled out. Huntley struggled to move the offense, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. Cleveland is now ahead of the Ravens in the division, and Baltimore wants to avoid a similar fate in Week 7 against Cincinnati. While the Ravens have won three of the last four games Huntley has started in place of Jackson, they are still just 7-12 without the star quarterback all time. It's unlikely that the Ravens would close as favorites, even at home, if Jackson were to miss the game against Joe Burrow and Co. in Week 7. This season, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. The Ravens star leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Baltimore's practice reports should give a better look into Jackson's status this week, but bettors should treat him as highly questionable until he is able to return to the practice field.
