McCarthy starting for Giants Bengals vs. Ravens bold predictions for AFC North clash in Week 7 Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:21 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Cincinnati Bengals , Ja'Marr Chase saved some money by appealing. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. One of Hendrickson's Baltimore Ravens teammates is drinking the Kool-Aid on this revenge game with a pretty big prediction: "Trey is a great leader, and he's a guy who flies around," linebacker Trenton Simpson said Wednesday. "And man, I am excited to see him against his former team. The things he's doing in practice, the way he rushed the passer, and just how he'd get off the ball. And I believe that this game for him is about to be like one of those multiple-sack games. So I'm calling it. I'm excited to see the celebration he does, so I'm excited." Hendrickson has missed two games this season with a broken finger that he got surgery on. If he were to have multiple sacks, it would be the first such performance with Baltimore, as he only has two sacks so far. He looked good last week against the Cleveland Browns, getting plenty of pressure on a rookie left tackle and recording a sack. It will be interesting to see how the Bengals scheme up pass protection with Hendrickson. One thing we know is the team will likely be excited to run directly at him. For years, one of the biggest knocks was that you could run at Hendrickson and gain yards pretty easily. It became more obvious as the defense deteriorated around him There is no doubt Hendrickson will be wearing the biggest chip on his shoulder. He was loud and clear about his displeasure with the front office, and he'd tell anyone who would listen about his offseason contract drama. That has clearly left a bad taste in most fans' mouths. Now, the Bengals will need to keep Hendrickson from having a big day if they are to come out of Baltimore with a W.

The Baltimore Ravens brought the veteran pass rusher in to make life miserable for opposing quarterbacks, and a divisional matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals gives him a chance to do exactly that. His former teammates know what he can do; however, the Ravens locker room is already expecting something special. Hendrickson has had a stop-and-start beginning to his Ravens career, with an injury keeping him out for part of the season. Now, with the Bengals coming to town on Sunday, one teammate has made a bold call about what could happen next. Trenton Simpson Expects Trey Hendrickson To Make The Bengals Pay Injured Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) talks on the bench with injured defensive end Trey Hendrickson (91) in the second quarter of the NFL Week 12 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the New England Patriots at Paycor Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 23, 2025. The Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson is predicting a multi-sack performance from Hendrickson against the Bengals, according to ESPN reporter Jamison Hensley , who shared Simpson's comments on October 21. The linebacker did not hide his excitement about seeing the veteran face his former team. Simpson pointed to what he's watched from Hendrickson during practice, particularly the way he gets off the ball and attacks opposing blockers. Those details have convinced him that a big afternoon could be coming. This is certainly a safe bet, particularly against the Bengals, who have Joe Burrow as their starting quarterback. Hendrickson played for five seasons with the Bengals team and emerged as one of the league's most feared edge rushers. He was the top sack leader in the NFL during the year 2024, and the Bengals team knows for sure what it means to face Hendrickson without any interference. Hendrickson showed some of his abilities even before playing against the Bengals. The Ravens saw Hendrickson play again on October 18 against the Cleveland Browns, where he recorded one sack and pressured the quarterback despite the Ravens losing 13-10. The reunion also carries some intrigue beyond the matchup itself. Hendrickson's departure from the Bengals f ollowed a contract dispute; however, there is no public indication that he's treating Sunday's game as a personal revenge mission. Veteran defensive lineman Calais Campbell a cknowledged that facing an old team can bring extra motivation while making clear that Hendrickson tends to keep his thoughts to himself. Colbie Young's return is imminent as well At wide receiver, rookie Colbie Young is also on track to returning very soon. Taylor said the 24 year-old looks “ as good as he has in a long time .” Young was close to playing in Week 5 against the Dolphins. He suffered his knee injury on the first offensive play of Cincinnati's Week 3 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. His injury pave the way for Mitch Tinsley to return to the club. His return would put the Bengals on the doorstep of being fully healthy at the position. Andrei Iosivas coming back would complete the group. Iosivas needs to sit out at least one more game before he's eligible to come off of I.R. The Bengals have not had their full receiving corps since Week 2. Two of those players, linebacker Swayze Bozeman and tight end Tanner Hudson, have been placed on the Reserve/Injured list. The other one is safety Kyle Dugger, who was declared as week-to-week with his quad injury. Dugger did practice for the first time in weeks Monday, signaling progress towards him being able to suit up in the near future. “I think he's progressing along,” Taylor said of Dugger Monday afternoon . “We'll kind of see where he's at.” Cincinnati has leaned on fellow backup S PJ Jules in the two games Dugger has missed. S Russ Yeast has also been elevated from the practice squad in Dugger's absence. Cincinnati will release its first injury report of the week on Wednesday. It sounds like it should be a relatively clean list to start the week. The main injury storyline for this week revolves around Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Baltimore lost its starting QB two weeks ago to an ankle sprain. Tyler Huntley is 1-1 in his place. When asked for an update on Jackson, Ravens coach Jesse Minter continues to label him as “ day-to-day ,” claiming he can “potentially” play Sunday against Cincinnati. He said that Jackson has made progress, but obviously wants to keep things vague early in the week. Jackson has won 11 of his 13 starts against the Bengals. away.headline: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out?
away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. LS Zach Wood (calf) returned from injured reserve and is expected to play. The Saints don't have another long snapper on the roster. home.headline: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants
home.blurb: Texans WR Tank Dell to return from gruesome 2024 knee injury on Sunday vs. Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel . Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here. Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings J.J. McCarthy starting for Giants Ryan Young Staff writer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. away.headline: Broncos have a real question about Bo Nix's future in Denver amid 2026 struggles
away.blurb: "Denver is good enough to keep winning despite Nix showing a limited ceiling," Fowler writes. "He is a quality starter but is not poised to enter the upper echelon. Confidence appears to be an issue this season, raising questions about what this player-term marriage looks like long term." Broncos have a real question about Bo Nix's future in Denver amid 2026 struggles | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV The 2025 Denver Broncos were one game away from making the Super Bowl with Bo Nix under center, but he suffered a brutally unlucky ankle injury in the AFC Divisional Round and missed the AFC Championship Game. But Nix was back and good to go for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. With a still-strong offense that added Jaylen Waddle and an elite defense, it seemed like the sky was the limit for the 2026 Broncos. But through six weeks, it's been far from ideal. Unfortunately, the biggest area of concern is with Nix. Once thought to be the future of the QB position in Denver, as ESPN's Jeremy Fowler highlights, the Broncos now have a very real question to answer about Nix's future in Denver amid his struggles this season. Broncos have a real Bo Nix question to answer this offseason Nix isn't playing well for the Broncos right now, and there are some real questions about whether he should be the QB of the future in Denver. While the offensive environment is certainly not ideal, he does have a solid supporting cast with Waddle, Courtland Sutton, and a great offensive line that should be good enough to give Nix a chance to thrive. McCarthy surge Instead, he's struggling right now, with his lack of any downfield offensive game being a major concern, especially after a rough game on Thursday Night Football. But one of the more concerning facets of Nix's game so far is his lack of rushing ability. He's not nearly as effective on the ground as he was before, and that combined with sub-par passing numbers, doesn't bode well for his future in Denver. While the Broncos have found a lot of success as a team with Nix at quarterback, he's not doing nearly enough right now to justify Denver spending $50-plus million per-year on him. So, what will the Broncos do with Nix in the future? Once seen as a no-brainer decision to give him an extension, Nix's 2026 struggles have drastically changed his outlook, with a future in Denver no longer guaranteed. away.headline: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper Eligible to Return from NFL Exempt List for Week 7 vs. Cardinals
away.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . The NFL removed Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt List on Friday. Cooper will be eligible to make his season debut during the Broncos' Week 7 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25. He was initially placed on the Commissioner's Exempt list on Aug. 30 and was barred from practicing or attending the team's games before he was reinstated. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.headline: Broncos injury report: Pat Surtain, Jonah Elliss, Talanoa Hufanga, Jonah Coleman updates
away.blurb: Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were limited while safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) and running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) did not participate. Surtain has missed the team's last two games, and it sounds like he might also miss Week 7 , but returning to practice is a good step in the right direction. Hufanga is likely going to miss at least one more game after sitting out last week's contest. Jahdae Barron and Taylor Rapp have done a nice job stepping up in the secondary while PS2 and Hufanga have been sidelined. Denver coach Sean Payton indicated Elliss avoided a season-ending injury , but he seemed to hint that Elliss could land on short-term injured reserve later this week. Meanwhile, Cooper is expected to return to the active roster this week after being reinstated by the NFL . Badie injured his thumb in the second quarter of last Thursday's game, and he was ruled out just before halftime. Meanwhile, Coleman is eligible to return from injured reserve this week, and he returned to practice on Wednesday, opening his 21-day window to be activated to the 53-man roster. Head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie's groin injury popped up after he "felt a little something" in his groin at the end of Thursday's practice. McDuffie did not practice Friday in what McVay indicated was a precautionary approach being taken. Safety Kam Curl (ankle) is also listed as questionable for Week 6, but McVay said they "feel good about him." McVay said Curl's ankle injury stemmed from "soreness" from Monday night's game against the Bills. McVay also said tight end Davis Allen (foot), who was limited in Friday's practice, is "trending in the right direction." Allen was later listed without a game status designation on Friday's injury report. home.blurb: Injury Report: Cardinals Officially Rule 3 Out, 4 Questionable vs Rams Skip to main content SI.COM The Cardinals are officially ruling out Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Wydett Williams (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) ahead of Week 6's battle at SoFi Stadium. Questionable for Arizona is all of Budda Baker (groin), Zaven Collins (hip), Kitan Crawford (ankle) and Blake Gillikin (back). Neither Baker or Collins practiced on Friday while Crawford and Gillikin did in limited fashion. For the Rams, both Kam Curl (ankle) and Trent McDuffie (groin) are questionable entering the weekend. Neither practiced on Friday for Los Angeles. "You got Jimmy Lake as kind of his right hand man in the defensive backfield, so there's definitely technique changes and different coverages and tools that they're using. Cardinals vs Rams Final Inactives: Who's In, Who's Out for Week 6 ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a lengthy injury report entering this weekend's clash with the Los Angeles Rams. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur dove deeper into Love's absence, which you can read about here . Off the Cardinals' injury report is all of Carson Beck (back), Devin Duvernay (ribs), Isaac Seumalo (rest) and Josh Sweat (rest). The likes of Davis Allen (foot), Alex Bachman (wrist), Tyler Higbee (rest), Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), Colby Parkinson (shoulder), Omar Speights (knee), Kegan Trost (hamstring), Josh Wallace (shoulder) and Byron Young (rest) were fully removed from Los Angeles' injury report and are good to go. It's a familiar battle for both sides entering the week, as LaFleur spent the last few seasons under head coach Sean McVay in Los Angeles as the team's offensive coordinator, putting him against Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula. "There's obviously familiarity with just going against him for two of the three years. First year was with Raheem [Morris], but that defense has evolved a lot over the last — since he took over to last year to this year. Obviously, similar foundations and characteristics, but they definitely put their new little twists on it," LaFleur said on facing Shula on Sunday. Both offensive units boast elite fantasy firepower, but division clashes always bring unique defensive tests and gamesmanship. If you are navigating lineup decisions ahead of Sunday afternoon's kickoff, here is a breakdown of which Lions fantasy superstars belong in your starting lineup, and which options require a bit more caution. Must-Start Locks Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (WR1) * The Outlook: St. Brown remains the unquestioned heart of Detroit's passing attack. Operating out of the slot, "The Sun God" provides a relentless target floor that thrives in fast-paced divisional battles. Green Bay's secondary has struggled at times against refined route runners over the middle. Expect Jared Goff to lean heavily on his favorite target to sustain drives, making St. Brown an elite WR1 in all PPR formats. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (RB1) * The Outlook: Gibbs' dual-threat dynamic explosion makes him virtually matchup-proof. With his elite speed on Ford Field's turf, he only needs a handful of touches to break open a slate. The Packers have surrendered chunk plays to explosive pass-catching tailbacks out of the backfield, giving Gibbs immense ceiling potential in PPR and half-PPR leagues. High-Upside Starts Jared Goff (QB) * Verdict: Solid QB1 Start * The Outlook: Goff inside the friendly confines of Ford Field is one of the safest fantasy plays on the board. At home, Goff operates Drew Petzing' system with supreme efficiency and rhythm. While Green Bay's pass rush can generate pressure, Goff's quick-release capabilities and weapons across the field give him a safe 18–22 point fantasy floor with multi-touchdown upside. Start with Caution / Situational Starts Jameson Williams (WR) * Verdict: High-Risk Boom-or-Bust Flex * The Outlook: Williams possesses game-breaking speed capable of turning a single target into a 70-yard touchdown. However, against Green Bay's deep safety coverage, target volume can be volatile. If you need pure upside to pull off an upset in your matchup, roll the dice on Williams; if you require a steady double-digit floor, explore alternative options. Sam LaPorta (TE) * Verdict: Low-End TE1 / High-End TE2 * The Outlook: LaPorta continues to command valuable red-zone attention, but increased target competition across the offense has capped his weekly target share. Green Bay's linebackers and safeties play tough physical coverage against tight ends over the middle. He remains startable given the top-heavy nature of the tight end position, but manage expectations accordingly. Final Lineup Verdict Lock in your top-tier Lions stars without hesitation. Detroit's high-octane offense inside Ford Field provides plenty of fantasy production to go around. Fire up St. Brown, Gibbs, Goff with confidence as Detroit aims to defend home turf against their division rivals.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Lions predictions: Detroit's biggest weakness could decide Week 7
picks.blurb: Detroit scores points like no other, but also gives them up at an alarming rate. In other words, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should be salivating at the matchup. The fantasy managers who roster those players will be thinking the same thing. More importantly, this is a key contest in the ever-crowded NFC North where there is no margin for error. Green Bay enters the contest at 4-2, erasing any negative thoughts that surfaced after the 0-2 start to the year. Detroit is 3-2, which is good enough for last place in the NFC North. Both teams are chasing the 5-0 Vikings , with the 4-2 Bears standing in the way as well. With only so many playoff spots to go around, this Week 7 matchup could have massive implications down the road. Here's a look at the keys to the game, injuries to watch and a prediction. Lions vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Lions -142; Packers +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions Keys To Victory Slow down Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. It's easier said than done, of course, but it's the one true path to victory for Detroit - outside of winning a shootout. The Lions' secondary has been a huge weakness all season long, and perhaps there is no better team position to exploit that than the Packers. Green Bay will try to hit some home runs with its speedy receivers. Even with Brian Branch set to return, Detroit will have to be willing to sit back in zone coverage and hold the visitors to some singles. Packers Keys To Victory Stay patient. With a defense as weak as the Lions, the Packers just have to play the waiting game. And that's something Dan Campbell's teams haven't been known to do. Detroit can either take away the long ball or attempt to get to Jordan Love with pressure. If the Lions sit back, then the Packers need to show an ability to run the ball. If they pressure, get ready to light up the scoreboard. Green Bay has the advantage, but it can't beat itself. Injuries to watch • S Brian Branch • OL Cade Mays • OL Aaron Banks. Lions vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 34, Lions 30 This game might come down to who has the ball last. Detroit might be coming out of the bye with some reinforcements, but this is still a defense that will ruin a season. And for that reason, no lead is safe - especially against the rival Packers, who can strike quickly. Jordan Love was forced to grow up as a quarterback without a running game to rely on through the first six weeks. He is passing that test with flying colors after a slow start. Trust the more well-rounded Packers to get the job done and push their winning streak to four. Adam Kaufman: Lions 31, Packers 27 This should be fun. Green Bay has won three straight, but Detroit comes out of its bye with reinforcements. Brian Branch's expected return won't magically fix the secondary, though even a few additional stops could make a significant difference. The Lions already have an offense capable of taking advantage, with Jahmyr Gibbs headlining their weapons. Jordan Love should still find opportunities, and the Packers can absolutely win if they protect him and avoid giving the home team extra possessions. Josh Jacobs' availability is another important piece. I'm expecting both quarterbacks to have productive stretches. But Jared Goff and Dan Campbell have been a dynamic duo with extended rest and know what's at stake in a crowded NFC North. This should be competitive well into the fourth quarter, but I like the Lions indoors. The Detroit Lions (3-2) will host their division rival Green Bay Packers (4-2) in Week 7, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -3.5 points . The Packers finished their 2025 season by snagging the seven seed in the playoffs, but the Bears eliminated them in the Wild Card round. Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley was hired to be the next head coach of the Miami Dolphins, and Green Bay hired Jonathan Gannon (previously the head coach of the Cardinals) as a replacement. With Gannon came a new 3-4 defense and a whole bunch of changes on the defensive side of the ball. EDGE Rashan Gary was traded to the Cowboys, NT Colby Wooden was traded to the Colts, while EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, MIKE Quay Walker, and CB Nate Hobbs departed in free agency. EDGE/LB Micah Parsons continues to recover from an ACL tear and is not expected to be available in Week 7. Being up against the cap, the Packers elected to promote from within, inserting EDGE Lukas Van Ness and ILB Isaiah McDuffie into the starting lineup, trading for LB Zaire Franklin (who is starting in place of injured Edgerrin Cooper), and drafting starters CB Brandon Cisse (second round) and NT Chris McClellan (third) on Day 2 of the NFL Draft. On offense, the Packers lost QB Malik Willis, RB Emanuel Wilson, WR Dontayvion Wicks (traded to the Eagles), WR Romeo Dobbs, LT Rasheed Walker, and LG/C Elgton Jenkins; like on defense, they elected to mostly promote from within, elevating RB Marshawn Lloyd into a bigger role (especially with Josh Jacobs suspended—he is expected to return in Week 7), WR Savion Williams and LT Jordan Morgan into the starting lineup, and shifting Sean Rhyan inside to center. Their guard spots have been a massive problem, and the Packers have been searching for answers, with their most recent pairing being RG Travis Glover and former Lion LG Laken Tomlinson (starting in place of the injured Aaron Banks). After a slow start to their 2026 season, the Packers have settled down as their offense has found its groove. The Packers opened the season with a loss after allowing the Vikings to drop 39 points on them, rebounded in Week 2 by beating the Jets by three points, only to lose again in Week 3 as the Falcons dominated them on the ground to the tune of 35 points. In Week 4, the Packers once again found a way to win by three points, this time over the Bucs, then smashed a Caleb Williams-less Bears team 31-7. In Week 6, the Packers took on the Cowboys’ 31st-ranked defense on “Sunday Night Football,” and while they jumped out to a 17-0 lead in the first half, they only scored six points in the second half. Fortunately, their defense held strong and allowed only 13 points, and the game ended in a 23-13 win. With the Packers offense in a groove, the Lions secondary is certainly going to be tested. Will they be able to carry over the success they had against the Cardinals in Week 5? Will Brian Branch return? If so, how big of a factor will he be? With so much unknown about the Lions’ defense, there’s a real chance the Packers continue their run of putting up points, and Detroit will need their top-scoring offense to keep pace and lead the Lions to victory. away.blurb: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur addressed Josh Jacobs’ return Wednesday, acknowledging the running back’s off-field legal troubles while expressing his belief in second chances. For now, the former Alabama standout is eligible to return, but his status for Sunday and potential league discipline remain unresolved. Jacobs returned to practice after missing Green Bay’s first six games while on the NFL’s Commissioner’s Exempt List. His reinstatement comes amid an ongoing league investigation into a domestic incident involving his former girlfriend. The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov shared a video on X, formerly Twitter, showing LaFleur discussing how the Packers balance welcoming Jacobs back with the seriousness of his legal case. The NFL placed Jacobs on the Commissioner’s Exempt List on August 30 before removing him on Monday. However, his removal does not conclude the NFL’s investigation under its Personal Conduct Policy. Additional discipline remains possible, and whether his six missed games will count toward a future suspension has not been finalized. Jacobs and the woman involved also filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent the release of evidence related to the incident. On the field, the Packers desperately need rushing production. Green Bay enters Sunday’s matchup vs. the Lions averaging an NFL-worst 59.8 rushing yards per game despite holding a 4-2 record and riding a three-game winning streak. home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers’ star quarterback, who has carried the load for most of the team’s 4-2 start, was deemed limited participation on Wednesday, the first day of on-the-field work before Sunday’s NFC North showdown at the Detroit Lions. Only one player, receiver Bo Melton (back), would not have practiced. Nine players were limited, including Love and receivers Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Christian Watson (ankle). The Lions are coming off their bye. Every player on the roster practiced, including safety Brian Branch, who is set to return from last year’s torn Achilles. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), QB Jordan Love (back), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle). Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows. Limited participation: CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring). Packers-Lions Wednesday Injury Report: Here’s What Jordan Love Said About Sore Back Skip to main content SI.COM GREEN BAY, Wis. – Jordan Love has taken a beating at times this season. For the first time, it’s shown on the injury report. He said “no” when asked if he was concerned that he will not be in the lineup against Detroit. Coming off a Sunday night game and with a Thursday night game looming against the Panthers, coach Matt LaFleur conducted a “jog-through” practice on Wednesday but will put the team in pads for a “really good” practice on Thursday. That was welcome news for Love. After two games of strong pass protection in wins over Tampa Bay and Chicago, it was another painful week for Love in the win over Dallas. “It’s just dealing with a sore back from the game,” he said. “Just some lingering effects from that. One of those things, we’ll just take it day by day but, obviously, it was nice to have a jog-through day, a little bit more mental day, and just recover.” By the official stats, Love and Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson have absorbed a league-high 45 hits through Week 6. He was hit eight times and sacked on three against the Cowboys. “Obviously, just with the back, I don’t know exactly what play it happened on, when it happened,” Love said. “We talk about all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket. That’s something that we’ve talked about, we harp on, and there’s been some better efforts to do better and protect better. I think guys are responding to that. It’s one of those things, yeah, you want to be able to limit as many hits as I take.” Running back Josh Jacobs, who is returning after six weeks on the exempt list, is not on the injury report. “I’ve been actually practicing with my helmet and shoulder pads, so it’s not like it’s overly different,” Jacobs said. “I don’t know where we’re going to be at this week, or if I’m actually going to play or not. home.headline: Packers Announce Concerning Jordan Love Injury News Before Lions Game
home.blurb: The Packers officially added Love to their injury report with a new back injury ahead of Sunday afternoon's game in Detroit and listed him as an estimated limited participant for their "jog-through" practice session on Wednesday, October 21. Who is Packers' Backup QB if Jordan Love Sits Out? The Packers are still a long few days away from being anywhere close to potentially ruling out Love for Week 7's road game against the Lions. Even so, it is worth examining their fallback plan at quarterback if Love's injury holds him out. The Packers would need to add Slovis to their 53-man roster to have him available as their emergency third quarterback against the Lions. They could also just elevate him and make him active, but that would leave three active quarterbacks — unless they become certain Love won't play. All four players were estimated limited participants for Wednesday's walkthrough. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) was also a limited participant as he continues to work through his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. Packers OC Makes Feelings Clear on Josh Jacobs Return Packers Trade Addition Put on Notice Amid Josh Jacobs Return Packers Announce Jordan Love Injury News Before Lions Showdown Unlock the latest Heavy on Packers news — direct to your inbox. The Green Bay Packers may have a mildly concerning quarterback issue brewing amid the latest Jordan Love news before Week 7's game with the Detroit Lions . Love played all 75 offensive snaps in the Packers' 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football in Week 6, but he did take three sacks during the matchup. Love — who is on the injury report for the first time this season — will have two more practices to improve his practice participation before the Packers must decide whether to list him with an injury designation on their final injury report. According to The Athletic's Matt Schneidman , though, Love said there is "no chance" he won't play against the Lions despite dealing with back soreness. Veteran Tyrod Taylor is the first-choice backup quarterback behind Love as the only other quarterback on the Packers' 53-man roster. He has made 19 starts and played more than 4,200 offensive snaps since coming into the league in 2018, but he has only played two regular-season snaps for the Packers in garbage time against Chicago. The Packers also have third-year quarterback Kedon Slovis on their practice squad. Right now, little suggests the Packers are worried that Love won't play against the Lions, but their roster moves at quarterback in the coming days could prove telling. If there are no moves, though, the chances of Love playing grow exponentially. Afterward, Los Angeles coach Sean McVay said, ""We won't win a game unless we figure out how not to beat ourselves." The Rams have lost three of their last four games, Myles Garrett is still recovering from a knee injury and now Los Angeles travels to Las Vegas to take on an improved Raiders ' team. Seattle (3-3) is back in the Sunday Night Football spotlight against unbeaten Kansas City, and this is a huge game for the Seahawks. Seattle also has lost three of its last four games, and quarterback Sam Darnold has struggled after returning from a hip injury. San Francisco (6-0) leads the NFC West with an unbeaten record, so it's on the Rams and Seahawks to catch up now. picks.headline: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams
picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. The Los Angeles Rams (2-4) visit the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday, October 25 (1:25 PM PT). The Rams have lost three of their last four, most recently 18-16 to Arizona on a field goal as time expired. The league’s top offense entering the week managed just 286 yards and turned the ball over twice in Cardinals territory in the fourth quarter. Davante Adams (knee) and kicker Blake Grupe (knee) were both hurt in the loss, and their status will be worth watching all week. Las Vegas has lost three straight, including a 33-30 loss to Buffalo in which Kirk Cousins threw for 313 yards and two touchdowns. Cousins is tied for the NFL lead with 14 touchdown passes. Odds and injury reports will change before kickoff, but here’s how our simulation models compare with the opening DraftKings prices. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots. home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
home.blurb: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal." Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season. While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum. "C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line." Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media. "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game." The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

Both of these teams have playoff expectations in 2026, but they’re in very different spots through six weeks of the season. Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs +2.5 (-115) Seahawks -2.5 (-105) Seahawks: -135 42.5 (Over -105/Under -115) The Seahawks opened as just 1.5-point favorites in Week 7 , but the line has already moved to Seattle -2.5. There is clearly some confidence in this Seattle defense with an extended rest at home against Kansas City. The Chiefs have not lost this season, but they are banged up at the receiver position with Rashee Rice missing Week 6 and Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Oddsmakers seem to think this is a spot where the Chiefs will lose their first game in 2026. Chiefs vs. Seahawks Betting Preview These are two of the best defenses in the league, which isn’t what you’d usually think about when referring to a Patrick Mahomes-led squad. The Chiefs traded away Trent McDuffie in the offseason, yet they’re third in the league in EPA/Play and success rate and fourth in EPA/Pass. That could be an issue for a Seattle team that is heavily reliant on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, especially since Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions already this season. Seattle (No. 2 in EPA/Play on defense) completely shut down Bo Nix and the Broncos in Week 6, but it wasn’t enough with this offense still struggling. Seattle is just 25th in EPA/Play and 20th in success rate on that side of the ball through six games. It makes sense that the defending champs are favored at home, but there is one stat that I can’t look past when it comes to Mahomes. He’s been a road underdog 12 times in his career, going 10-1-1 against the spread and 9-3 straight up. The Chiefs look like one of the best teams in the NFL, and I expect that to remain the case in Week 7. I don’t mind getting 2.5 points with them as an early lean for this primetime matchup. Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs trade acquisition in line for his first start as offensive line injuries linger into first practice for Week 7 vs. Seahawks
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs could trot out a third starting offensive line combination of the 2026 NFL season in Seattle. Wednesday’s practice offered few encouraging signs for a pair of injured tackles. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed Wednesday that starting right tackle Jaylon Moore remains in the NFL’s concussion protocol . Moore must clear the league’s return-to-play protocols to suit up against the Seahawks. According to Reid, he would not participate in Wednesday’s practice. What Are the NFL’s Return-to-Play Protocols for Concussions? Players placed in the NFL concussion protocol must complete five phases without symptoms before they can be cleared to return to play. Symptom-limited activity: Light stretching and stationary bike riding. It remains to be seen whether Moore can clear those protocols ahead of the Week 7 matchup. However, sitting out of practice entirely on Wednesday isn’t a good start. So who is in line to start at right tackle? Fans would hope starting left tackle Josh Simmons could return to the lineup after he practiced in a limited capacity ahead of Week 6’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. That didn’t look promising on Wednesday. Reporters didn’t spot Simmons on the field during their brief look at team stretch and warm-ups. Reid also didn’t mention Simmons’ status when he addressed injured players. He spoke only about Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice, who also did not practice. Simmons did return to practice in a limited capacity last week. Still, clips captured during the brief window the team gives media members ahead of practice made it clear Simmons wasn’t 100%. He was seen grimacing while stretching , and he simply didn’t look right while jogging on the field. It very much looks like the back injury will keep him out longer. Reid’s comments on Monday suggested the Chiefs are continuing to work through his back issue while ramping up his workload. Again, missing practice Wednesday doesn’t set him up for a likely Week 7 return. The Kansas City Chiefs may field their third starting offensive line combination of the season when they travel to Lumen Field to face the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football” in Week 7. Kansas City has started only two different offensive line combinations so far. The second came in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders, when Mike Caliendo started at left guard for Kingsley Suamataia . Now, after another offensive line injury in Week 6, the Chiefs will likely start a new right tackle against Seattle. away.blurb: Chiefs CB L'Jarius Sneed Makes Unexpected Offer to Fan Following Return From Injury Sneed entered Sunday's AFC West matchup listed as questionable because of a knee injury. However, the 29-year-old was not listed as inactive before kickoff, making him available for the divisional game. Sneed's availability was significant given the injuries that limited him during his two seasons with the Tennessee Titans . His return also came during a significant offseason overhaul of Kansas City's cornerback group. K ansas City Chiefs cornerback L'Jarius Sneed is earning praise from fans after making a special offer to a supporter who attended the team's 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers . Sneed, who recently returned to action after a knee injury, responded to a fan on X who wanted his No. 38 jersey as a birthday keepsake. The fan, who uses the handle @joeyv18, attended Sunday's game at Arrowhead Stadium to celebrate turning 38 and shared a photo of Sneed walking toward the locker room with his teammates. "Longshot but was at the Chiefs game sunday celebrating my 38th Birthday was hoping to get that Sneed 38 jersey to commemorate the trip!" the fan wrote . Sneed quickly responded, offering to help. "I gotcha, dm me your address or P.O. Box," the cornerback replied. Chiefs supporters praised his willingness to help make the fan's birthday memorable. L'Jarius Sneed's Birthday Gesture Draws Praise From Chiefs Fans Several fans responded to Sneed's message, praising the veteran cornerback for taking time to acknowledge a supporter. One fan wrote, "So much respect for @jay__sneed for this one of my favorite chiefs, since he was a rookie." Another added, "You sir, are the man! That is badass that you would do this for a fan. A true Chief through and through!" Other responses included, "Sneed is a man of the people!" and "What a great dude. True to the Kingdom!" The exchange came shortly after Sneed was cleared to play against Los Angeles despite appearing on the injury report. Chiefs Cornerback Returns From Knee Injury Against Chargers Kansas City defeated Los Angeles 22-6, remaining undefeated following its early-season bye week. After Kansas City traded him to Tennessee in 2024, the cornerback signed a four-year, $76 million contract. However, injuries prevented him from establishing a consistent role with the Titans. Sneed appeared in just 12 games over two seasons in Tennessee. He began the 2025 season on the physically unable to perform list while recovering from a knee procedure and a lingering quadriceps injury. The cornerback eventually returned and appeared in seven games, recording 26 tackles and three passes defended. away.headline: Kenneth Walker Reacts to Revenge Game vs. Seahawks, Patrick Mahomes Talks Chiefs RB's Return
away.blurb: Walker will return to Lumen Field for the first time since his Super Bowl LX MVP run with the Seahawks this Sunday. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said he expects Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks to be "special" for Kenneth Walker III shortly after the running back downplayed his own focus on reuniting with his former teammates. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him," Mahomes told reporters Wednesday. "You go back to the place where you built your career, where you won a Super Bowl. I know how special that is being here. Those fans are the people that were around him for all of that. Those are a still a lot of the guys that were his teammates that he grew up with, as well, as in the NFL." Mahomes concluded, "At the end of the day, you've got to win a football game. He knows that we have his back." Walker previously declined to add similar gravity to the situation when asked after the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday whether it would feel "different" to play against the Seahawks. "We've got to go critique the mistakes that we made," Walker said about the Week 6 win. "And then, once we get to that point, we'll see." Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Wednesday he felt Walker would take a "level-headed" approach to the matchup even if he receives special attention from the Seahawks defense. "The one thing that, when you're on a team, everyone knows your strengths and weaknesses... I'm sure the boys there will try to get after him a little bit," Reid said . "He's a pretty level-headed guy... he's kind of got one speed. He's coming at you, and it doesn't really matter who he's playing, where he's playing." The Chiefs agreed to a three-year, $43 million deal this offseason with Walker, who The Athletic's Michael-Shawn Dugar reported Wednesday did not receive an offer from the Seahawks ahead of hitting free agency. Walker has since rewarded the Chiefs for making him one of the NFL's highest-paid running backs by racking up a league-high 665 rushing yards with six touchdowns through five games. The Seahawks, which have so far this season deployed one of the NFL's top run defenses, will be tasked with limiting Walker for the first time since drafting him in 2022 when the Week 7 matchup kicks off Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET.

home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs trade acquisition in line for his first start as offensive line injuries linger into first practice for Week 7 vs. Seahawks
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs could trot out a third starting offensive line combination of the 2026 NFL season in Seattle. Wednesday’s practice offered few encouraging signs for a pair of injured tackles. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid confirmed Wednesday that starting right tackle Jaylon Moore remains in the NFL’s concussion protocol . Moore must clear the league’s return-to-play protocols to suit up against the Seahawks. According to Reid, he would not participate in Wednesday’s practice. What Are the NFL’s Return-to-Play Protocols for Concussions? Players placed in the NFL concussion protocol must complete five phases without symptoms before they can be cleared to return to play. Symptom-limited activity: Light stretching and stationary bike riding. It remains to be seen whether Moore can clear those protocols ahead of the Week 7 matchup. However, sitting out of practice entirely on Wednesday isn’t a good start. So who is in line to start at right tackle? Fans would hope starting left tackle Josh Simmons could return to the lineup after he practiced in a limited capacity ahead of Week 6’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. That didn’t look promising on Wednesday. Reporters didn’t spot Simmons on the field during their brief look at team stretch and warm-ups. Reid also didn’t mention Simmons’ status when he addressed injured players. He spoke only about Moore and wide receiver Rashee Rice, who also did not practice. Simmons did return to practice in a limited capacity last week. Still, clips captured during the brief window the team gives media members ahead of practice made it clear Simmons wasn’t 100%. He was seen grimacing while stretching , and he simply didn’t look right while jogging on the field. It very much looks like the back injury will keep him out longer. Reid’s comments on Monday suggested the Chiefs are continuing to work through his back issue while ramping up his workload. Again, missing practice Wednesday doesn’t set him up for a likely Week 7 return. The Kansas City Chiefs may field their third starting offensive line combination of the season when they travel to Lumen Field to face the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football” in Week 7. Kansas City has started only two different offensive line combinations so far. The second came in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders, when Mike Caliendo started at left guard for Kingsley Suamataia . Now, after another offensive line injury in Week 6, the Chiefs will likely start a new right tackle against Seattle. Football-specific exercise: Non-contact drills and football movement. Club-based non-contact drills: Full football practice with no contact. home.headline: Kenneth Walker Reacts to Revenge Game vs. Seahawks, Patrick Mahomes Talks Chiefs RB's Return
home.blurb: Walker will return to Lumen Field for the first time since his Super Bowl LX MVP run with the Seahawks this Sunday. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said he expects Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks to be "special" for Kenneth Walker III shortly after the running back downplayed his own focus on reuniting with his former teammates. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him," Mahomes told reporters Wednesday. "You go back to the place where you built your career, where you won a Super Bowl. I know how special that is being here. Those fans are the people that were around him for all of that. Those are a still a lot of the guys that were his teammates that he grew up with, as well, as in the NFL." Mahomes concluded, "At the end of the day, you've got to win a football game. He knows that we have his back." Walker previously declined to add similar gravity to the situation when asked after the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday whether it would feel "different" to play against the Seahawks. "We've got to go critique the mistakes that we made," Walker said about the Week 6 win. "And then, once we get to that point, we'll see." Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Wednesday he felt Walker would take a "level-headed" approach to the matchup even if he receives special attention from the Seahawks defense. "The one thing that, when you're on a team, everyone knows your strengths and weaknesses... I'm sure the boys there will try to get after him a little bit," Reid said . "He's a pretty level-headed guy... he's kind of got one speed. He's coming at you, and it doesn't really matter who he's playing, where he's playing." The Chiefs agreed to a three-year, $43 million deal this offseason with Walker, who The Athletic's Michael-Shawn Dugar reported Wednesday did not receive an offer from the Seahawks ahead of hitting free agency. Walker has since rewarded the Chiefs for making him one of the NFL's highest-paid running backs by racking up a league-high 665 rushing yards with six touchdowns through five games. The Seahawks, which have so far this season deployed one of the NFL's top run defenses, will be tasked with limiting Walker for the first time since drafting him in 2022 when the Week 7 matchup kicks off Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET.

Before last week, Simmons hadn't practiced since Aug. 16. Asked about his potential status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Reid was hesitant to overpromise. The team will continue to ramp up Simmons' workload and see how he responds as he returns from injury. The Chiefs could realistically be without two of their most experienced offensive tackles, Moore and Simmons. That would leave Kahlil Benson as the starting left tackle and Joshua Ezeudu as the starting right tackle. Diego Pounds would also be active for the first time since Kansas City acquired him in a trade , should Moore be out with his concussion. Reid discussed Ezeudu's Week 6 performance on Monday. I thought he did a nice job there. So, and he's got experience. I'm not real worried about all that.” In 17 pass-blocking snaps on Sunday , Ezeudu allowed just one hurry per Pro Football Focus. The Chiefs put him in a good spot to be successful in that game. With a full week of practice and preparation as a potential starter, Ezeudu could deliver an even better performance against Seattle. Before the season started, this looked like a potential swing game for the NFC East standings, but a lot has changed in six weeks. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Mauricio Rodriguez Tue, October 20, 2026 at 9:05 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys are reshuffling both the 53-man roster and the practice squad before a must-win Monday Night Football matchup. One special teams standout is finally getting his reward. The Dallas Cowboys made multiple roster moves ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles. The changes touch both the 53-man roster and the practice squad, and they include a quarterback. At 2-4, Dallas can't afford to waste a roster spot right now. These moves reflect that, from depth at quarterback to rewarding a core special teamer. Cowboys add Kyle Trask to the practice squad The Cowboys are signing quarterback Kyle Trask to the practice squad. Dallas carried three quarterbacks until the Eagles poached Joe Milton off the practice squad last week. Trask now fills the spot Milton left behind. You might remember Trask from his college days with the Florida Gators. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft. He has since spent time with the Atlanta Falcons and the Carolina Panthers, and Carolina released him as part of its final roster cuts before the regular season. This is Trask's return to the NFL. Don't expect him to push for QB2 snaps, though. Trask has appeared in seven games in his NFL career and attempted only 11 passes across those appearances. Despite his second-round pedigree, he has never really gotten a chance to play in a major way. He has spent most of his career as a backup. For the Cowboys, this move is about depth. They like to carry three quarterbacks, and signing Trask gives them a 28-year-old option in case it's ever needed. Sam Howell remains the backup behind the starter. Howell beat out Milton in the preseason quarterback battle, and nothing about the Trask signing changes that. Juanyeh Thomas earns a spot on the 53-man roster Here's the move that might matter most on Sundays (or Monday, in this case). Dallas is signing Juanyeh Thomas to the 53-man roster after elevating him from the practice squad three consecutive times. Teams can only lean on elevations for so long, and Thomas has made the decision an easy one. He has become a core special teamer. In the Cowboys' Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers, Thomas played 95% of the special teams snaps. The week before, on Thursday Night Football, he logged 91% of them. Those numbers tell you how much the coaching staff trusts him on that unit. That's why he's getting a permanent spot. Caelen Carson's time in Dallas comes to an end Thomas' promotion comes at the expense of cornerback Caelen Carson. The Cowboys drafted Carson out of Wake Forest in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. The hope was that he would bring flexibility to the cornerback room, with the versatility to play both inside and outside. It never worked out. Carson never looked like the player Dallas thought it was getting out of college. When he did play, it was mostly out of necessity, and a rough preseason in August didn't help his case. Now he's out of the picture only three years into his Cowboys career. We'll see where he lands next. These moves set the stage for Monday Night Football against Philadelphia, and the stakes couldn't be much higher for the Cowboys. At 2-4, this is a must-win game. The good news is that the NFC East seemingly has no team interested in winning it at this point. Nobody has grabbed control of the division, and that leaves the door open even for the lowly Cowboys. The Cowboys are trying to be the team that rises above all of their problems. Whether they can pull it off starts with the Eagles. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week.
