away.headline: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers
away.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday. away.headline: Four players questionable, two out for Dallas Cowboys; will Micah Parsons play?
away.blurb: Cornerback Cobie Durant will miss his fourth consecutive game and backup offensive tackle Drew Shelton will miss a second consecutive game with hamstring injuries, as both were ruled out on Friday. Even though head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Friday that linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a “long shot” to play with a hamstring injury of his own, he was officially listed as questionable after logging limited participation in back-to-back practices this week. He has missed four games since suffering the injury in Week 1. Trade acquisition cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has been battling an ankle injury that limited him in practice on Wednesday and Friday. He was a full participant on Thursday. Fellow cornerback Ameer Speed has been battling a knee issue this week, but he was able to log back-to-back limited practices to finish the week. Both are officially listed as questionable. Rotational rookie defensive tackle LT Overton popped up on the injury report on Friday with a foot injury that prevented him from practicing. He is also listed as questionable. A quartet of players will not play for the Packers on Sunday night, as defensive tackle Jonathan Ford (calf), defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (achilles), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) were all ruled out on Friday. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley is working his way off the injured reserve list with an achilles injury, but he was ruled doubtful to be activated ahead of Sunday night. Five more players were listed as questionable, as defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip), interior offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quad), guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and wide receiver Savion Williams (ankle) will all be gametime decisions. Williams will need to be activated off injured reserve on Saturday to have a shot at playing. He will not be activated in time for Sunday night’s game and will instead be watching his current and former team square off from the sideline. He is expected to return in early November. home.headline: Report: Eagles will not be punished by NFL for handling of Jalen Hurts blood clots
home.blurb: It was revealed Monday that Hurts will be out indefinitely after multiple clots were discovered in his lungs. The news came two days after Hurts was placed on injured reserve — despite initial reports stating the team wouldn’t place him on IR — and four days after last week’s announcement that he had a blood clot in his calf. “I fully trust the people that are involved in helping us all make these decisions,” Sirianni said. “We have great people here. … The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them. “Don’t have much more to say about that. That’s why we put the statement out. Full trust in those guys … kind of feels like you’re questioning that, and I know you guys have a job to do, but I’ve got the relationship with the players that I have because of the time that we spend together and because of the care that we have for each other. So, it’s always at the forefront of our mind.” The Eagles won’t face any heat from the NFL for their handling of Jalen Hurts’ potentially season-ending injury. The NFL concluded, in news first reported by The Athletic and later confirmed by the Associated Press, that the Eagles clearing Hurts to play in Week 5 despite having a superficial blood clot in his calf was “handled appropriately.” The league will not be issuing any punishment for their handling of the medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation for the game. Later on Tuesday, the NFL Players Association issued a statement: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” The Eagles’ medical staff has faced scrutiny from fans and media for its handling of the Hurts situation. Coach Nick Sirianni gave the team’s medical staff a vote of confidence Monday but declined to expand on the specifics of Hurts’ injury process. ©2026 The Philadelphia Inquirer. Visit inquirer.com. home.headline: Eagles steal QB from Cowboys: Joe Milton expected to sign with Philadelphia after injury to Jalen Hurts
home.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Imagn Images With Jalen Hurts out this week due to a blood clot , the Philadelphia Eagles ended up stealing a player from the Dallas Cowboys . The Eagles are going to sign Joe Milton off of the Cowboys' practice squad, according to multiple reports . Under NFL rules, if you sign a player off another team's practice squad, that player has to be placed on your 53-man roster, so Milton won't be a practice squad player in Philadelphia; he'll be on the actual roster. With the addition of Milton, that means the Eagles will have three quarterbacks heading into Sunday's game against Carolina. Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton . Hurts has already been ruled out due to a blood clot in his calf and it's unknown when he can return to the field. For Sunday, the Eagles will hand the starting job over to McKee , but clearly, they weren't comfortable with only having a rookie behind him, which is why they went out and added Milton. There was some speculation that the Eagles might look to bring Andy Dalton back to Philadelphia, but in the end, the team decided to go with Milton. During the 2026 offseason, the Cowboys made a trade for Sam Howell , and he ended up beating Milton out for the backup QB job. The Cowboys ended up cutting Milton after the preseason in a move that seemed to blindside the 26-year-old QB. The fact that the Eagles are adding a quarterback likely signifies that Hurts will be out for more than one game. If they thought he was only going to be out for a week, they probably would have been comfortable with Payton as the backup for just one game, but if Hurts is going to miss an extended amount of time, then it certainly makes sense to add another quarterback, which is what Philly ended up doing. The Eagles didn't go into detail about the nature of the clot that Hurts is dealing with, but ESPN has reported that he'll be out indefinitely "until this situation is solved." At this point, it seems like almost a given that the Eagles will end up putting Hurts on injured reserve. If they DON'T go that route, that means they'd have to carry four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, which wouldn't make sense for a team that currently has 24 players on its injury report.
